summary: Graphic EQ 10, 20 and 30 bands, distortion and de-esser in Score, and one filter-kind table so 17 processors reach a document instead of 4
target:
All code facts below were read at c4d06841. Paths are under `crates/`. Spec lines are `master-spec-v02.229/spec-modules/14-studio-creative-suite.md`.

**The gap.** The truth check (`research/truth-check-20261105-mt-video-audio-design-web.json`, top_missing rank 5) finds no graphic EQ, no distortion and no de-esser in Score. The audit did not name a second gap, which this lane also closes: a processor in Score does not reach a document unless one adapter knows it. `hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/audio_batch.rs:43-55` `EffectSpec` has four kinds, and `:819` refuses every other `filter_kind`. Every document path goes through it: bus and master (`audio_session.rs:86-111`, `pulse/src/bus_mix.rs:62` and `:15` say pulse knows no processor kinds), waveform effects (`waveform.rs:476-486`), batch and presets (`audio_batch.rs:509-529`), keyframe range lookup (`timeline/audio.rs:383-392`). So `Reverb`, `FeedbackDelay`, `Flanger`, `Chorus`, `Phaser`, `HardLimiter`, `HumRemover` and `ClickRepair` are tested in Score and a document cannot use them. After this lane a stored `filter_kind` reaches 17 kinds instead of 4.

The spec gives the graphic EQ family full parameter tables (STU-FX-136a line 18727; GraphicEQ10Bands 18824-18842, 20 bands 18844-18872, 30 bands 18874-18912). DeEsser (19057) and Distortion (19062) have catalogue rows with 0 parameters and no table.

Suggested identifiers below are not product names; the `filter_kind` keys follow `audio_batch.rs:662` (score's processor identity tags).

1. **Red first.** New test files in `hsk-studio-score/tests/`: `graphic_eq.rs`, `distortion.rs`, `deesser.rs`, `filter_kinds.rs`; and `hsk-studio-harness/tests/audio_filter_kinds.rs` starting `#![cfg(feature = "audio-batch")]` (round unit `["audio-batch"]` exists, `.config/round-features.toml:34`). Prove them red by running. A pushed red commit must compile, so give the new API refusing stubs first. Use `tests/common_dsp.rs` helpers (`bounded_case`, `run_blocks`).

2. **Graphic EQ kernel, new `src/graphic_eq.rs`.** One processor with a band count of 10, 20 or 30. Second-order peak sections in `f64`, transposed direct form II with the 1e-30 flush of `filters.rs:67-79`. `Equalizer` is not the base: it stops at `MAX_EQ_SECTIONS` 16 (`eq.rs:17`), and its cookbook form (`eq.rs:64-119`) has no control of the gain at the band edge, which this design depends on. Do not change `Equalizer`. Method: Liski and Valimaki, The Quest for the Best Graphic Equalizer, DAFx-17, https://www.dafx17.eca.ed.ac.uk/papers/DAFx17_paper_94.pdf. Read sections 4 and 5 before coding; re-derive, copy no third-party code.

| Fact | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Section | `H(z) = (1 + G b - 2 cos(w) z^-1 + (1 - G b) z^-2) / (1 + b - 2 cos(w) z^-1 + (1 - b) z^-2)`; `b = tan(B/2)` at G = 1, else `sqrt(abs(GB^2 - 1) / abs(G^2 - GB^2)) tan(B/2)`; `GB = 10^(c g / 20)` | paper eq. 1 and 2 |
| Prototype gain | `g_p = 17` dB | paper, octave and third-octave |
| `c` | 0.3 at 10 bands, 0.4 at 30 bands. 20 bands: not published. Sweep 0.3..0.4 in 0.01 steps, pin the best, record the table in lane notes | paper; 20 bands authored |
| Bandwidth | Choose `B` per band so the prototype response equals `c g_p` at the lower neighbour's centre (the lowest band uses its upper neighbour), by bounded bisection at construction (at most 60 steps per band). The paper states the plain form `B = 1.5 w` at octave spacing and adjusts the top bands because the response turns asymmetric; one rule for all bands holds at every rate | paper; uniform rule is this brief's reading |
| Interaction | `M = 2 N - 1` design points (centres and geometric means, paper 19 by 10 and 61 by 31); `B[m][k] = 20 log10 abs(H_k(w_m)) / g_p`; least squares through the pseudoinverse | paper |
| Iteration | One: rebuild the matrix from the gains of the first pass, solve again. Near-zero band gains keep the prototype shape (`abs(g) < 1e-9`: G = 1) | paper; the near-zero rule is this brief's |
| Target at midpoints | Mean of the two neighbouring commands in dB. UNVERIFIED against the paper's text extraction; check it when reading | this brief |

Band centres are authored (the spec declares none; vendor bands UNVERIFIED, D5): 10 bands `1000 * 2^k`, k = -5..=4 (31.25..16000 Hz, the paper's set); 20 bands `1000 * 2^(k/2)`, k = -11..=8; 30 bands `1000 * 2^(k/3)`, k = -16..=13. A centre at or above 0.95 Nyquist is dropped, the rule of `restore.rs:601`; its row stays stored; `active_bands()` reports the count and the matrix uses only active bands. No active band leaves master gain only.

Proof, through `magnitude_db()` (shape of `eq.rs:205`) and a real-time sine check at three bands agreeing with it within 0.01 dB:
- All amps and gain 0: bit-exact identity (the promise at `eq.rs:138`).
- Worst band-centre error at most 1.0 dB at 44100 and 48000 Hz: all 1024 settings of +-12 dB at 10 bands (the paper's own search); at 20 and 30 bands all +12, all -12, zigzag, and 200 seeded binary settings. If a set exceeds 1.0 dB, stop and send the numbers. Do not loosen the bound. The paper measured 31 bands; 30 is UNVERIFIED until this runs.
- `amp` above +-12 dB has no accuracy claim. Single band +-70, zigzag +-70 and every band +70 with gain +64 stay finite and stable at every test rate: 8000, 32000, 44100, 48000, 96000, 768000 (a pole check plus an impulse decaying below 1e-6 of its peak).
- Bit-identical for any block partition; `save_state`/`restore_state` continue bit for bit (`state.rs`, the promise of `bus.rs:178-183`), the state holding the applied coefficients and the design counter.

Cost: a lane ramp sets a parameter before every sample (`session.rs:13-16`). One design here is a matrix rebuild and a solve, far too much per sample. So `set_automated` stores the command and marks it dirty, and `process` designs at most once per `DESIGN_HOP` frames, counted from stream start (default 256, `layout.rs:18` `CANCEL_CHECK_FRAMES`). Declare this in the docs and DESCRIPTOR: band automation takes effect at the hop, not at the sample. Master `gain` applies at once. A set before frame 0 designs at frame 0, so `tests/automation.rs:204-214` still holds. A test counts designs: a ramp over 8000 frames does at most 32. No allocation in `process` or a design (`engine.rs:9-11`): work matrices are allocated at construction. Measure and record the design time in debug and release.

3. **Parameter records, `src/spec_rows.rs`.** STU-FX-136b (18732) and MT-32629..32631: each row stores hard_min, hard_max, soft_min, soft_max, default, unit and precision as separate values, and an unknown stays unknown, never mirrored (STU-FX-107 line 12839). Add a typed record with `Option` fields, plus slot, normalised default and mapping (STU-FX-121 line 12998; `normalised_to_value` at `dsp.rs:10`), and a const table for the three sheets, row for row:

| Parameter | Slot | hard_min | hard_max | default | default (normalised) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| accuracy | in0 | 10 | 8192 | 999.997454 | 0.120997 |
| gain | in1 | -64 | 64 | 0 | 0.5 |
| range | in2 | 1.5 | 120 | 47.808615 | 0.39079 |
| amp1..ampN | in4..in(3+N) | -70 | 70 | 0 | 0.5 |

soft_min, soft_max, unit and precision are absent on every row. A test reads the table: row counts 13, 23 and 33 (catalogue 19101-19103), slot order, and `normalised_to_value` of each normalised default equals the default within 1e-3 (the sheet rounds its normalised column). Add `from_normalised` on the pattern of `HardLimiterParams::from_normalised` (`dsp.rs:337`).

Add the rows to `SPEC_ROWS` (`spec_rows.rs:40`): `gain` and `amp*` bound, naming dB as authored. `accuracy` and `range` are `Err(NO_MEANING)`: the spec gives each a name and a range and no meaning. They are accepted, range checked and stored, and change no sound. A public vendor manual suggests FIR length for `accuracy` and slider travel for `range`, but that is not spec text and was not read at source. See open_questions. `tests/multiband.rs:221` already walks every row.

4. **Distortion, new `src/distortion.rs`.** No spec parameters, so all are authored and named so in the module doc, as `multiband.rs:19-20` does. `drive_db` 0..48, `curve` Soft (`tanh`) or Hard (clip at +-1), `mix` 0..1, `output_db` -48..0. Waveshaping with first-order antiderivative antialiasing (Parker, Zavalishin, Le Bivic, DAFx-16): `y[n] = (F(x[n]) - F(x[n-1])) / (x[n] - x[n-1])`, and when the difference is under a stated epsilon `f((x[n] + x[n-1]) / 2)`. `F` of `tanh` is `ln cosh`; write it `abs(x) + ln((1 + exp(-2 abs(x))) / 2)` so it cannot overflow. `F` of Hard is `x^2/2` inside and `abs(x) - 1/2` outside. Automatable: `drive_db`, `mix`, `output_db`. `mix` 0 with `output_db` 0 is bit-exact input. The wet path is half a sample late; `latency_samples` stays 0, and the docs state it. Proof: a 5 kHz sine at 24 dB drive has less energy off the harmonic series than a test-only plain waveshaper, by at least 6 dB (a floor to confirm by running; record the measured figure; `SpectrumAnalyzer` at `spectrum.rs:17` with a bin-centred tone); odd harmonics only for Soft on a symmetric input within a stated floor; wet output bounded by `10^(output_db/20)` plus a stated tolerance, including input at `f32::MAX`; partition independence; `save_state`.

5. **DeEsser, new `src/deesser.rs`.** No spec parameters; authored as in item 4. `frequency_hz` 2000..16000, refused `OutOfRange` at or above 0.95 Nyquist; `threshold_db` and `ratio` with the ranges `DYNAMICS_THRESHOLD_DB` and `DYNAMICS_RATIO` (`dynamics.rs:18-19`); `attack_ms`, `release_ms`; `split_band` boolean; `link`. Reuse `Crossover` (`multiband.rs:74-104`, one per channel) and the `Dynamics` gain computer (`dynamics.rs:264` `detect`, `:280` `step`, both `pub(crate)`). The detector reads the high band. Split band: `out = low + gain * high`. Broadband: `out = gain * (low + high)`. Automatable: `threshold_db`, `ratio`; `frequency_hz` fixed at construction, as multiband crossovers are. Latency 0. Proof: below threshold the magnitude is flat within 1e-9 (the allpass of `multiband.rs:11`); 8 kHz at -6 dB, threshold -30, ratio 4 settles at `static_reduction_db` (`dynamics.rs:146`) within 0.1 dB of the band-level prediction; 500 Hz in the same run moves under 0.1 dB in split mode and by the full reduction in broadband; partition independence; `save_state`. This is catalogue row MT-32662, `AudioFilter:DeEsser`. MT-32292 (17581) is a different row, engine `ae_native`, 6 parameters; do not claim it.

6. **Filter-kind table in Score, new `src/filter_kinds.rs`.** Score has no Folio edge and must not gain one. A const table of rows: `filter_kind`, spec studio effect and import key where the row has one, and parameters (key, default, score automation index or none). `build_audio_filter(filter_kind, params: &[(&str, f64)], rate, channels) -> Result<Box<dyn Automatable + Send>, AudioFilterError>`. The error is a typed enum with `code()` like `SpecRowError` (`spec_rows.rs:18-33`): unknown kind, missing parameter, unknown parameter, not a whole number, or `Score(ScoreError)`. Do not add `ScoreError` variants.

Enumerations and booleans are declaration indices, as `audio_batch.rs:694-697`. Whole-number fields (`voices`, `stages`, `harmonics`, `ar_order`, enumerations) are checked before any cast (`pick`, `audio_batch.rs:689`): 1e308, -1, 2.5 and NaN are refusals. 7. **Document reach, `hsk-studio-harness-view/src/view/audio_batch.rs` and `mixer.rs:106-120` only.** Add one variant holding `filter_kind` and params, delegating to item 6 in `build` (`:58`), `build_automatable` (`:71`), `automation_index` (`:87`), `to_preset_instance` (`:698`) and `from_preset_instance` (`:751`). G near GB at tiny gains divides 0 by 0 and yields NaN coefficients. Control: abs(g) < 1e-9 means G = 1, and a test at 1e-12 dB.
Half-sample wet delay combs a distortion at mix 0.5 at high frequencies. Control: stated in docs, a test pins the response at mix 0.5.

patterns_found: Cascade of one second-order peak section per band with an interaction matrix, least squares and one iteration; reported error under 1 dB at +-12 dB commands.
Bandwidth set by the gain at the neighbouring centres, not by a -3 dB rule; top bands adjusted for asymmetry.
First-order antiderivative antialiasing with a fallback at small differences; it adds half a sample of delay.
De-essers: high-pass or band-pass detector, then broadband or split-band reduction; 4 to 10 kHz is the usual zone.
reuse_opportunities: score: Crossover, Dynamics detect and step, SosState flush, normalised_to_value, StateWriter, SpectrumAnalyzer for proofs, tests/automation.rs kinds.
harness-view: the existing EffectSpec paths mean one new variant reaches bus, master, waveform, batch and presets.
rejected_options: Linear-phase FIR with accuracy as its length: gives the row a meaning, but the spec does not declare it, it adds latency up to about 4096 samples, and per-sample lane ramps would redesign and reconvolve; also needs partitioned convolution first.
Cookbook peaking sections with fixed Q and no correction: neighbouring bands add up; the paper's subject is that error.
Raising MAX_EQ_SECTIONS and reusing Equalizer: the cookbook form lacks band-edge gain control, and existing records and tests pin its bound.
Symmetric band filters with weighted least squares (Ramo 2020): better published error, heavier design; full text not read. A later improvement if measured error requires it.
Oversampling for distortion: adds latency and a filter; antiderivative form keeps latency 0.
One more EffectSpec variant per kind: repeats five match arms per kind in a paused crate; the table belongs in Score, with no egui reach.
Convolution Reverb first: larger, and blocked on an asset reference in the stored instance.
